step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture depicts Graham Media Group's digital broadcast and live video streaming pipeline on AWS. Systems Manager controls on-premises camera encoders via remote commands. Live contribution streams from the encoders are ingested into AWS Elemental MediaStore. MediaStore forwards live video to MediaLive for distribution encoding, and simultaneously pushes a copy to S3 for long-term archiving. MediaLive feeds MediaPackage to package video streams for various target consumer devices, which are then distributed via CloudFront. Archived media in S3 is processed asynchronously by Rekognition for facial and content identification, and Transcribe for generating automated captions.

nodes.name: Systems Manager
nodes.notes: Automates on-premises local encoders via SSM agents and Lambda execution scripts.

nodes.name: On-Prem Encoders / Camera
nodes.notes: On-premises camera equipment and hardware video encoders at local TV stations.

nodes.name: Media Store
nodes.notes: Receives the live contribution stream from on-prem encoders.

nodes.name: Media Package
nodes.notes: Packages video streams into formats suitable for multiple device types (phones, HDTV, Web).

nodes.name: CloudFront
nodes.notes: CDN for delivering media packages to end-user devices.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Permanent archive storage for all shot video content.

nodes.name: Rekognition
nodes.notes: Performs facial recognition and scene tagging on archived video.

nodes.name: Transcribe
nodes.notes: Generates automated captions directly for the video content.

edges.notes: Systems Manager automates equipment, ad breaks, and camera switching on local encoders.
On-prem encoders push live contribution video stream to MediaStore.
MediaStore streams video payload to MediaLive for distribution encoding.
MediaLive sends encoded multi-bitrate video streams to MediaPackage.
MediaPackage delivers formatted video streams to CloudFront CDN for global end-user streaming.
MediaStore writes video archives directly to S3 bucket.
S3 archive video is read by Rekognition for visual tagging and face search.
S3 archive audio/video is read by Transcribe for automatic subtitle and caption generation.
